stories.headline: Micron's next-generation 3D NAND to double bit density with over 400 layers, offering extreme performance
stories.claim: Micron unveils G11 3D NAND, due for mass production in the second half of 2027, with roughly double bit density.
stories.summary: Micron has revealed its next-generation G11 3D NAND at an event, with mass production planned for the second half of 2027. The company says the chip will roughly double bit density over its current G9 generation, raise I/O speeds by up to 50% and cut data transfer energy per bit by more than 25%. It will use wafer-on-wafer bonding, letting the memory array and peripheral logic be built on separate wafers, and will exceed 400 NAND layers. Micron also said it is developing new materials and denser cell architectures to keep scaling beyond G11, though it has not disclosed post-G11 details. The improvements are aimed at both high-capacity SSDs and AI-oriented storage.
key_points: Micron's G11 3D NAND is due to enter high-volume production in the second half of 2027.
The company targets roughly twice the bit density of its G9 generation.
I/O performance is expected to rise by up to 50%, with data transfer energy per bit cut by more than 25%.
G11 adopts wafer-on-wafer bonding, a technique also used by rival YMTC, and exceeds 400 layers.
Micron plans further detail in 2027 and is developing new materials and cell architectures beyond G11.
The products target client and data centre SSDs and AI storage demand.
stories.market_take: Mainly a product roadmap announcement; limited near-term effect on memory stock prices.

stocks.reason: Company's next-generation NAND roadmap strengthens its competitive position in storage.

stories.headline: Andy Burnham says he has emergency stockpile of beans, soup and Twiglets
stories.claim: PM Andy Burnham says he keeps emergency supplies at home as the government launches a household preparedness campaign.
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he keeps beans, soup and Twiglets in case of a civil emergency, in response to the government's Be Ready campaign. The campaign advises households to keep at least three days of supplies, including bottled water and long-life food, for events such as extreme weather or cyber-attacks. Burnham said the advice was not a reason for panic buying and was long-term rather than urgent. Defence secretary Wes Streeting cited the threat of state-sponsored terrorism by Russia or other hostile powers against everyday infrastructure. Treasury minister James Murray said he had not yet followed the advice himself and that the UK was catching up with countries such as Ireland, France and the Netherlands.
key_points: The government's Be Ready campaign advises households to hold at least three days of water and food.
Burnham said he has beans, soup and Twiglets at home and stressed it is not about panic buying.

stories.headline: Telegraph ‘to cut up to 100 jobs’ in plans to become ‘AI-powered media business’
stories.claim: The Telegraph begins a consultation on cutting up to 100 jobs as it restructures towards an AI-powered media business.
stories.summary: The Telegraph Media Group has started a formal consultation over plans to cut up to 100 jobs, with sports and culture departments particularly affected. The cuts are part of a strategy to turn the paper into a global, AI-powered premium media and intelligence business. Chief executive Carolin Hulshoff Pol said the paper had limited ability to invest during its sale process and that the organisation needs clearer accountability and faster decisions. The title was acquired by Axel Springer for £575 million, completed in June after three years of uncertain ownership. Axel Springer, which also owns Politico and Business Insider, aims to accelerate digital transformation and expand further into the US.

stories.headline: Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia
stories.claim: Ukrainian drone strikes are repeatedly closing Moscow-area airports, and analysts discuss the risks to civil aviation.
stories.summary: Drone strikes by Ukraine have forced near-daily closures of Moscow's Domodedovo, Sheremetyevo, Zhukovsky and Vnukovo airports in October, according to Agentstvo, with some closures lasting up to nine hours. Zelenskyy announced in September that Ukraine would seek to make Russian airspace unsafe, and Kyiv warned the International Civil Aviation Organization. Analysts quoted by DW say Russia's emergency 'carpet' protocol could shut airspace widely and that heightened risk could push insurers to raise rates sharply. They also warn that Russian air defence missiles pose a risk to civilian aircraft, recalling the 2024 Azerbaijan Airlines crash that killed 38 people. Foreign airlines' decisions will depend on the military threat, demand and insurance costs.
key_points: Moscow's four main airports have reportedly closed almost daily in October due to drone strikes.
Some closures reportedly lasted up to nine hours.
Zelenskyy said in September that Russian airspace would become unsafe for airlines and insurers.

stories.market_take: Limited direct listed-stock impact; higher aviation insurance and fuel-related costs would mainly affect airlines serving Russia.

stories.headline: Queen Letizia’s Dress Highlights Pyratex Recycled Lyocell Fabric
stories.claim: Queen Letizia wore a dress made from Pyratex recycled lyocell fabric, developed with Circ's textile-to-textile recycling, at the Princess of Asturias Awards.
stories.summary: Queen Letizia of Spain wore a dress at the Princess of Asturias Awards in Oviedo made from Pyratex Circ Lyocell 3, a knit fabric containing recycled cellulose recovered from discarded textiles. Pyratex says the fabric was chosen before the garment was designed, guiding its construction. The fibre is 30 percent recovered textile cellulose and 70 percent wood pulp, and Circ's hydrothermal process separates cotton-derived cellulose from polyester. Pyratex and Circ have worked together for three years, and the companies have previously supplied fabrics for collaborations with Mara Hoffman, Zara and H&M Group. The appearance highlights the growing use of recycled textiles in high-profile fashion.

stories.headline: CFTC Charts Federal Path for Retail Crypto Transactions and Cryptoasset Markets
stories.claim: The CFTC has issued a proposal that could bring leveraged and fully paid retail crypto trades under its regulation.
stories.summary: The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission has issued an advance notice of proposed rulemaking setting out a possible federal framework for retail crypto transactions. It proposes two rules, Regulation CTX and Regulation CAM, and uses Section 2(c)(2)(D) of the Commodity Exchange Act as the legal basis. A key preliminary view is that a platform-wide offer of leverage could bring even fully paid crypto purchases under CFTC oversight. If a platform registers as a designated contract market, it would also be preempted from state money-transmitter laws, according to the Commission's preliminary view. The document is a request for public comment and contains no draft regulatory text.
key_points: The CFTC has issued an advance notice of proposed rulemaking on retail crypto transactions.
It proposes Regulation CTX and Regulation CAM under Section 2(c)(2)(D) of the CEA.
Even fully paid trades could fall under the rules if a leveraged offer is available on the platform.
Exchanges would need designated contract market status, with state money-transmitter laws preempted in the Commission's view.
The notice seeks public comment and does not yet include proposed rule text.
stories.market_take: Could bring large crypto exchanges under CFTC rules, a mixed outcome for exchange operators and a potential boost for compliant platforms.

stories.headline: Typhoon Champi kills one and injures more than 500 in Taiwan as it heads to China
stories.claim: Typhoon Champi killed one person and injured over 500 in Taiwan before weakening and heading towards the Chinese coast.
stories.summary: Typhoon Champi, once classified as a super typhoon, swept past Taiwan on Saturday, killing one man swept away by waves off Liuqiu island and injuring 527 people. The storm uprooted trees and cut power to more than 167,000 homes, most of which had been reconnected by the time of reporting. Taiwan's Central Weather Administration said the system was weakening, with gusts of around 126km/h near its centre, and it was about 150km east of the island. Northern and central Taiwan, including Taipei, extended office and school closures for a second day and some flights were still cancelled. The storm is forecast to turn north towards China's coast and later move into southern Japan.

stories.headline: Father who killed Oregon school shooter describes anguish over children he couldn't save
stories.claim: A father who shot dead the gunman at an Oregon school describes his anguish over the children he could not save.
stories.summary: Kaylub Giamanco, a 36-year-old carpenter, described his actions in an interview with Oregon Public Broadcasting after he shot and killed a 16-year-old former pupil who attacked Silver Rail Elementary School earlier this month. Three students and a teacher were killed, and six people were shot in total. Giamanco said he followed the gunman into the building, crawled through a window and fired at him in a classroom where a teacher was struggling with the attacker. He said he now relives the attack and feels he could not save everyone. Oregon Governor Tina Kotek praised his intervention, and his family has asked for privacy. Police identified the gunman as a former pupil with special education needs, and his motive remains under investigation.

stories.headline: On a Paris Island, an Art Museum Finally Takes Shape
stories.claim: Le Large, a new contemporary art centre on Île Seguin near Paris, has opened in the former Renault factory site.

stories.headline: This $56.2 Million Monet Painting Set a New French Auction Record

stories.headline: Boris Acket unveils his largest Einder to date at Amsterdam Dance Event
stories.claim: Dutch artist Boris Acket has opened EINDER, a large weather-driven fabric installation, at Amsterdam's Centrale Markthal during ADE.
stories.summary: Dutch artist Boris Acket has unveiled EINDER, his largest installation to date, at Amsterdam's Centrale Markthal as part of the Amsterdam Dance Event's 30th anniversary. A vast fabric canvas is suspended in the hall and moves in sequences informed by weather data from storms around the world. Acket used Claude Code to build a 3D simulation of the space and tools that translate weather data into fan and light controls. The work is on view from 22 October to 1 November 2026, and its movement is never the same twice.
key_points: EINDER is Acket's largest work to date, shown at Amsterdam's Centrale Markthal.
The fabric moves according to sequences drawn from global storm weather data.
Acket used Claude Code to build a 3D simulation and control tools.
The simulation helps him test ideas before installation, but site conditions still shape the outcome.
The installation runs from 22 October to 1 November 2026, during the ADE 30th anniversary.

stories.headline: Backlog at China’s Ports Was Finally Shrinking. Typhoon Champi Will Test That.
stories.claim: Typhoon Champi threatens the slow recovery of China's port backlogs, though major container terminals had not closed as of Friday.
stories.summary: Typhoon Champi is disrupting eastern China, with ferry suspensions and maritime emergency responses in Shanghai, Fujian and Zhejiang. No major container terminal closures were reported, but Seko expects temporary gate suspensions and pilotage halts at several ports from Friday night to Monday. The storm also closed work and customs across Taiwan. Port waiting times had been falling after Golden Week, but Sea-Intelligence data showed very poor schedule reliability in China earlier this autumn. Analysts expect congestion to take months to clear.

stories.headline: Middle East Physical Crude Slides While Brent Hits Five-Month High
stories.claim: Physical Middle East crude prices are falling even as Brent futures hit a five-month high of $114 a barrel.

Brent futures, however, jumped to a five-month high of $114 a barrel, which the article says reflects fears of escalation rather than physical supply. The piece also references a US drawdown of its strategic petroleum reserve and a US naval blockade of Iran, indicating a tense supply backdrop.
key_points: Brent crude futures reached a five-month high of $114 a barrel this week.
Physical Middle East grades such as Basrah Medium have fallen to deep discounts against Dubai.

stories.headline: Hospital in Yemen’s Taiz warns of collapse in days because of Houthi siege
stories.claim: A Houthi siege of Taiz is pushing the city's hospitals, including dialysis services, towards collapse.
stories.summary: Hospitals in the government-held city of Taiz, Yemen, are warning of collapse because of a renewed Houthi siege that began in early October. The Republican Hospital's dialysis centre, which treats 270 patients, has cut sessions from four hours to two and a half and may shut within days. Diesel and medical supplies are critically low, with diesel bought on the black market at five times its earlier price. The WHO has warned that 42 health facilities in Taiz city report severe shortages, and Amnesty International has called for roads to be reopened. Across the governorate, around 1,110 kidney failure patients are at risk.

stories.summary: US stock futures were mixed after a sharp chip selloff on Thursday. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.6% and the S&P 500 fell 1.21%, while the Dow closed nearly flat. LAM Research's CEO flagged supply chain constraints into 2027, which weighed on Nvidia, Micron and AMD. The semiconductor ETFs fell sharply, and Bloom Energy dropped nearly 9% after weak Q3 results. Tensions with Iran are rising, with Brent crude near $114 a barrel and WTI around $100. Investors are awaiting big tech earnings and a Federal Reserve decision next week.
key_points: The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.6% and the S&P 500 fell 1.21% on Thursday after a chip selloff.
LAM Research said supply chain constraints would keep limiting chipmakers into 2027.
Brent crude traded near $114 a barrel and WTI near $100 as Iran tensions escalated.
Bloom Energy shares fell nearly 9% after third-quarter results raised capex and cash flow concerns.
Investors are waiting for big tech earnings and a Federal Reserve decision next week.
stories.market_take: Chip weakness, higher oil and the upcoming earnings and Fed decision add near-term volatility to equities.

stories.headline: Kindle Unlimited is now Kindle Plus, and Amazon is betting big on AI audiobooks

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine trade attacks following US envoy visit
stories.claim: Russia and Ukraine traded heavy attacks after US envoy Witkoff met Putin; trilateral talks may resume in mid-November.
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged attacks overnight, with Moscow saying Ukraine launched 630 drones, 163 of them approaching the capital. Strikes in Kyiv wounded 15 people and damaged metro infrastructure. The attacks followed a three-hour meeting between US envoy Steve Witkoff and Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg, which Witkoff called constructive. The Kremlin said Russia was in principle ready to resume trilateral talks with the US and Ukraine in mid-November, after the US midterms. A summit between Putin, Trump and Xi Jinping is reportedly being prepared in Shenzhen for next month. The US has delayed new sanctions on Russia, a move linked to securing the release of a US citizen, and a diesel deal with Moscow has drawn criticism in Kyiv and Europe.

stories.headline: Gap Inc. Gets an AI Assist for Seasonal Hiring
stories.claim: Gap Inc. says its AI hiring assistant Bridgette is being scaled up to manage seasonal recruitment for the holiday season.
stories.summary: Gap Inc. has expanded Bridgette, an AI-enabled virtual career guide launched in June, to handle seasonal hiring across its Gap, Old Navy, Banana Republic and Athleta brands. stories.headline: Google Chrome will let you know if a website 'doesn't seem right' with these updates
stories.claim: Google is rolling out stronger Chrome Safe Browsing warnings, a ClickFix defence and Gemini-based scam alerts.
stories.summary: Google has announced updates to Chrome's Safe Browsing protections, available when Enhanced Protection is turned on, on desktop and Android. Suspicious sites will trigger a pop-up in the address bar saying the site 'doesn't seem right', while sites known to be malicious will show a full-screen red 'dangerous site' warning. Chrome will also block users from copying and running suspicious commands, a tactic known as ClickFix. Gemini-powered alerts will flag scams, spam and unwanted notifications, and users can mark a warning as safe if it is wrong.

stories.headline: Geoff Mann · What’s the truth? Prediction Markets
stories.claim: An essay examines how prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket work and the legal questions over whether they are gambling.
stories.summary: A London Review of Books essay by Geoff Mann examines prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket, which let users buy 'Yes' or 'No' contracts on future events. It uses the example of George Santos, who manipulated a Kalshi market on his attendance at a State of the Union address and was fined and banned for life. The piece explains how contract prices reflect probabilities and questions the claims that these markets are more accurate than polls. It also notes that most contracts are sports-related and that several US federal court cases, likely heading to the Supreme Court, will determine whether they count as gambling or federally regulated derivatives.
key_points: Kalshi banned George Santos for life after he manipulated a market on whether he would attend Trump's State of the Union address.
Prediction market share prices move between 1 and 99 cents according to the crowd's view of the probability of an outcome.

Kalshi and Polymarket argue they are regulated derivatives markets, not gambling businesses.
Gambling is regulated by individual US states, producing an uneven legal picture that several federal cases must resolve.

stories.headline: Christa Pike’s IV team warned vein might be ‘blowing’ before failed execution
stories.claim: A lawyer's new declaration details doubts among Tennessee's execution team during Christa Pike's failed lethal injection on 30 September.
stories.summary: A declaration from Randy Spivey, lawyer for death row prisoner Christa Pike, gives a minute-by-minute account of her failed execution in Tennessee on 30 September. The IV team spent almost an hour trying to find a vein, repeatedly voiced fears that the vein might be 'blowing', and used up to 10 needles. Pike survived the pentobarbital dose and was later returned to prison; she is reported to be the only prisoner in modern times to survive a full lethal injection dose. Governor Bill Lee has called off executions in the state pending a review, and the new filing is part of a legal challenge to Tennessee's lethal injection protocol.
key_points: Lawyer Randy Spivey's declaration describes the IV team's repeated doubts about whether the vein had been found.
The search for a vein began at 6.35pm and the team left assuming the procedure was on track, but Pike was still alive.
Pike spent 10 days in hospital and is back in prison, with her long-term prognosis unknown.
Governor Bill Lee has halted all executions in Tennessee pending a review.
The filing forms part of a challenge to Tennessee's lethal injection protocol, also tied to a failed execution in May.

stories.claim: Deckers Brands shares fell after its fiscal Q2 2027 sales missed forecasts, and it cut its full-year sales outlook while raising EPS guidance.
stories.summary: Shares in Deckers Brands, parent of Hoka and Ugg, fell more than 8% in after-hours trading after the company reported fiscal second-quarter 2027 net sales up 3.5% to $1.48 billion, which missed analyst expectations of $1.50 to $1.52 billion. Diluted EPS of $2.31 beat forecasts, helped by $46.0 million of IEEPA tariff refunds plus $3.0 million of interest. Hoka sales rose 6.8% and Ugg rose 3.5%, while direct-to-consumer sales fell. Deckers cut its full-year sales guidance to $5.70 to $5.73 billion but raised its diluted EPS range to $7.80 to $7.95, and named Rati Sahi Levesque to its board.
key_points: Net sales rose 3.5% to $1.48 billion, below analyst expectations of $1.50 to $1.52 billion.
Diluted EPS was $2.31, ahead of expectations, helped by tariff refunds.
Hoka sales rose 6.8% to $677.2 million, while Ugg rose 3.5% to $786.4 million.
Direct-to-consumer sales fell 1.8%, with comparable DTC sales down 6.4%.
Full-year sales guidance was cut to $5.70 to $5.73 billion, while EPS guidance was raised to $7.80 to $7.95.
Rati Sahi Levesque joins the board from 1 December.
stories.market_take: Shares fell after the sales miss and lower revenue outlook, though the tariff-boosted profit beat limits the damage.

stories.headline: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires
stories.claim: Fire union says firefighters and public were knowingly put at risk by underfunding during this summer's Welsh wildfires.
stories.summary: The Fire Brigades Union says firefighters and the public were knowingly put at risk during this summer's wildfires in Wales because of chronic underfunding. Crews reported shortages of pumps and appliances, inadequate kit such as unsuitable boots and clothing, and injuries that were described as commonplace. A control room worker said call volumes reached nearly 2,000 on the busiest day, against a usual 200 to 300. The FBU puts the shortfall at 400 firefighters in Wales, and a survey found 69% of firefighters felt significantly under-equipped. The Welsh government says fire authorities set their own budgets and should take the summer into account, and the First Minister is hosting a resilience summit in Merthyr Tydfil.
key_points: The FBU says firefighters were knowingly put at risk during this year's wildfires due to chronic underfunding.
Crews reported a lack of pumps and appliances, and some were using unsuitable boots and clothing.
The union puts the shortfall at 400 firefighters in Wales; 69% of surveyed firefighters felt significantly under-equipped.
A control room worker said calls peaked near 2,000 in a day, against a usual 200 to 300.
North Wales Fire and Rescue Service is seeking £500,000 from the Welsh government's emergency scheme to cover wildfire costs.
The First Minister is hosting a climate change and resilience summit in Merthyr Tydfil; a UK committee has called for a national wildfire prevention campaign.

sources.title: Firefighters and public 'knowingly put at risk' during summer wildfires

stories.headline: Bukang-i is back: famous shark returns to canal in South Korea hours after being coaxed out to sea
stories.claim: Viral dusky shark Bukang-i returned to a Busan canal hours after being guided out to sea, and a fresh rescue attempt is under way.
stories.summary: A dusky shark nicknamed Bukang-i, which has been stuck in a canal in Busan since 18 September, swam back into the waterway overnight after workers guided it out to sea on Wednesday. Officials are now making a fresh attempt, removing a screen, replacing a net and raising an outer barrier. Earlier attempts using water jets and nets had failed, and the shark has drawn more than 1.6 million visitors. Experts warn it may die within two weeks because of hunger, colder water and injuries, and officials say it appears to have difficulty balancing. Environmental groups link the shark's presence to warming seas.

Hubbard had been jailed after being convicted of fighting for Ukraine, and the US had designated him wrongfully detained. The release coincided with a meeting in Saint Petersburg between envoy Steve Witkoff and Vladimir Putin about new US proposals to end the war in Ukraine. Trump says the US gave nothing in return, but the report notes a series of recent US moves seen as favourable to Russia, including agreeing to buy sanctioned Russian diesel. stories.headline: Number of active emerging market funds holding the index’s top three stocks doubles
stories.claim: Trustnet finds active emerging market funds increasingly hold the index's top three stocks, driven by AI memory chip rally.
stories.summary: Trustnet research finds that the number of active emerging market funds holding the MSCI Emerging Markets index's top three stocks has doubled in a year. stories.headline: Rio Tinto eyes a giant hot-brick battery to cut fossil fuel use
stories.claim: Rio Tinto and Rondo Energy begin a study into a heat battery to supply steam at the Yarwun alumina refinery in Queensland.
stories.summary: Rio Tinto and California-based Rondo Energy have started engineering and design work on a heat battery at Rio Tinto's Yarwun alumina refinery near Gladstone, Queensland. The system would store cheap midday electricity in refractory bricks and release it as steam after dark. Rio Tinto estimates it could supply around 5% of the refinery's steam needs and cut direct emissions by about 67,000 tonnes of CO2 a year. The Australian Renewable Energy Agency is providing A$3.6 million for the study, with up to A$38 million for deployment if the project proceeds. A feasibility study is expected to take about 12 months.

stories.headline: I tried ChatGPT's latest Chrome upgrade and it surprised me
stories.claim: OpenAI has upgraded its ChatGPT Chrome extension with a sidebar, multi-tab access and ChatGPT Work for interacting with websites.
stories.summary: OpenAI has upgraded its ChatGPT Chrome extension, adding a sidebar that works alongside open webpages and can draw on information across multiple tabs. Through ChatGPT Work, the tool can also interact with websites on a user's behalf, such as filling in forms or organising tabs, with the user able to review before submitting. The reviewer tested the form-filling feature on a webinar registration page and found it useful but needing supervision. The upgrade places ChatGPT in more direct competition with Google's Gemini, which Google is building more deeply into Chrome. Users must install the extension and grant permissions, and access to ChatGPT Work depends on their account.
key_points: The updated ChatGPT Chrome extension adds a sidebar that can sit alongside the webpage being viewed.
It can read and compare information across multiple open tabs once permissions are granted.
ChatGPT Work can carry out tasks such as sending messages, filling forms and downloading files in Chrome.
The reviewer found form-filling useful but still needed a final human check before submission.
The move increases competition with Google's Gemini, which is being integrated more deeply into Chrome.
Advanced features depend on the user's account access.
stories.market_take: Modest competitive signal in the browser AI race; limited direct effect on listed stocks.

stocks.reason: ChatGPT's Chrome push competes with Gemini's built-in position in Google's browser.

stories.headline: While Micron Calls The 4F² Memory Cell Architecture A “Myth,” YMTC Has Followed CXMT In Lining Up A Prototype That Operates At 9,600 MT/s
stories.claim: Micron calls 4F² DRAM cell scaling a myth, while YMTC and CXMT pursue 4F² prototypes.
stories.summary: Micron's president and chief technology and product officer, Scott DeBoer, said at a technology webinar that 4F² memory cell architecture has no viable scaling path and that its density advantage over 6F² is somewhat of a myth. By contrast, China's CXMT plans to introduce a DDR5 RDIMM based on 4F² before the end of 2026. A Counterpoint Research report says YMTC is developing a 4F² prototype operating at 9,600 MT/s, with mass production planned at its Fab 3. Both Chinese firms are also exploring high-k metal gate technology to overcome lithography constraints.

Micron said it has researched 4F² for over 20 years without finding a viable scaling path.
CXMT plans to launch a DDR5 RDIMM based on 4F² before the end of 2026.

YMTC's mass production of this version is planned at Fab 3, according to the report.
Both Chinese firms are exploring high-k metal gate technology to offset DUV lithography limits.
stories.market_take: Technology divergence between Micron and Chinese rivals may matter for long-term memory pricing and share.

stories.headline: AI firms say UK has a year to head off datacentre protests before construction is threatened
stories.claim: AI industry taskforce urges UK government to create a 'compact' with local communities to head off datacentre opposition.
stories.summary: A taskforce called the Sovereign AI Leadership (SAIL) group, which includes Nvidia, Microsoft and Cisco, has asked the Labour government to create a compact offering local communities greater benefits from datacentres. It warns the UK has roughly 12 months to avoid US-style opposition that has halted projects. Proposals include letting councils keep more business rate revenue and an indicative contribution scaled to site size. Opponents, including PauseAI UK, Action to Protect Rural Scotland and Foxglove, criticised the plans. The government said it has already allowed councils in AI growth zones in England to keep all extra business rates and that community benefits are considered through local planning.

It warns the UK has about 12 months to build public consent before US-style opposition takes hold.

Campaigners argue the plans amount to buying off communities and would cost central government funds.

stories.headline: Australia is forcing Apple to loosen its grip on iPhone app distribution
stories.claim: An Australian court ordered Apple to open iOS to rival app stores and payment systems from March 2027; Apple plans to appeal.
stories.summary: Australia's Federal Court has ordered Apple to open iOS to alternative app marketplaces and payment services from 1 March 2027. The order follows an August 2025 finding that Apple misused its market power in app distribution and payments. Developers would be able to use competing payment providers, link to external checkouts and face limits on Apple's fees for eligible purchases. Apple has told Reuters it will appeal and seek a pause in enforcement, arguing the changes raise intellectual property and security concerns. Unless the court delays implementation, the rules will take effect in March 2027.

The new rules are due to take effect on 1 March 2027 unless a court delays them.

stories.market_take: Apple could see reduced App Store fee income in Australia over time, though the impact is small and the appeal may delay it.

stories.headline: Apple Reportedly Boosts iPhone Duo Orders by 44%
stories.claim: Apple reportedly raised its iPhone Duo foldable production target by about 44%, to 14 million units over 12 months.
stories.summary: DigiTimes reports that Apple has told Foxconn and component suppliers to raise its iPhone Duo foldable production target by roughly 44%, from 9.7 million to 14 million units. The revised figure reportedly covers a full 12-month period and follows strong pre-orders. Apple has described demand as extraordinary, and U.S. shipping estimates reached 25 January within 30 minutes of pre-orders opening on 16 October. DigiTimes warns that meeting the higher target could be difficult, given earlier reports of problems with assembly, displays and hinges. The device launches on 23 October at $1,999 in the United States.
